page: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Edsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a large 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1D cache. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Additionally, it includes a 236 GB local NVMe SSD and supports Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-threaded capabilities, with gzip compression reaching 34.96 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.44 GB/sec. However, multi-threaded performance is more constrained, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scoring in the weak category. Memory bandwidth tests show an average read-only rate of 44.69 GB/sec for large blocks, but write speeds and small-block cached reads are relatively weak. Database operations under Passmark are also on the lower end, though Redis SET operations maintain an average throughput of 7.86 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4ds_v7 offers a dense memory profile and fast local NVMe storage without the overhead of a high vCPU count, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is well-suited for relational databases, caching layers like Redis, web serving, and lightweight single-threaded data processing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 32.0 GB of RAM, and a 236 GB local NVMe SSD. The x86_64 architecture includes a large 480 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX. Benchmarks indicate strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, alongside average web serving and Redis throughput, though multi-core scaling and memory write bandwidth are relatively weak. This configuration provides a cost-effective balance of high memory density and local solid-state storage for workloads that do not demand extensive parallel compute. It is best suited for memory-intensive applications, caching layers, and relational database workloads.
